lead.headline: Hardware Supply Chain Compromise Exposes $91M Ledger Theft as Crypto's Most Critical Unpriced Risk
lead.tldr: This week revealed that physical supply chain attacks on hardware wallets now rival smart contract exploits in scale, while traditional finance integration accelerates through Mastercard stablecoin rails and Circle's EU regulatory milestone—creating a widening gap between institutional-grade infrastructure and retail security assumptions.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, this week the industry's most trusted security layer—hardware itself—proved compromisable at scale, even as institutional on-ramps gained regulatory clarity and traditional payment giants built stablecoin bridges.

top_signals.title: Inside the $91M Ledger Reseller Wallet Theft
top_signals.summary: A massive theft of $91M occurred after tampered Ledger hardware wallets were sold through a reseller called CryptoBilis. The devices contained hidden implants that captured recovery phrases, highlighting critical vulnerabilities in the hardware supply chain.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $91M Ledger reseller theft reveals hardware supply chain as an unpriced systemic risk: investors have underwritten smart contract audit risk for years while assuming physical custody devices were outside the attack surface, a gap that now demands repricing across wallet infrastructure and custody valuations.

top_signals.title: Binance.US seeks $1B valuation in potential $100M funding round: Report34m
top_signals.summary: Binance.US is reportedly seeking a $1 billion valuation as it explores a potential $100 million funding round. This move comes as the exchange navigates ongoing regulatory challenges in the United States.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Binance.US seeking $1B valuation on a $100M round while navigating unresolved US regulatory exposure tests whether offshore capital will price American regulatory uncertainty as temporary friction or permanent impairment.

top_signals.title: Criminals stole $90mn of crypto by hiding password readers in USB-like devices
top_signals.summary: Criminals stole $90 million in cryptocurrency using sophisticated USB-like devices that acted as password readers to compromise secure wallets. Ledger described the incident as one of the most advanced attacks the industry has encountered.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $90M USB-like password reader attack confirms that physical-layer sophistication is escalating faster than user education, implying consumer hardware wallet TAM may compress until manufacturers can cryptographically verify device integrity from factory to unboxing.

top_signals.title: Mastercard brings stablecoin balances into traditional banking and card payments 19m
top_signals.summary: Mastercard is integrating stablecoin balances into traditional banking and card payment systems. This move aims to bridge the gap between digital assets and mainstream financial infrastructure for easier spending.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Mastercard integrating stablecoin balances into traditional banking rails signals that payment incumbents are now building the infrastructure to abstract blockchain complexity entirely, which reprices value capture toward distribution and compliance layers rather than protocol tokens.

top_signals.title: EBA designates Circle’s USDC as the EU’s first 'significant' e-money token
top_signals.summary: The European Banking Authority (EBA) has designated Circle's USDC as the first 'significant' e-money token in the EU. This move shifts direct oversight of USDC's reserves and liquidity to the EBA starting November 12.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The EBA designating USDC as the EU's first 'significant' e-money token with direct reserve oversight starting November 12 creates a regulatory template that will concentrate compliant stablecoin issuance among entities able to afford bank-grade supervision, accelerating consolidation.

top_signals.title: Bitget, Liquid exploits push Q3 crypto hacks toward $1.2B
top_signals.summary: Crypto hacks in Q3 surged by 55% compared to the previous quarter, totaling nearly $1.2 billion. The majority of these losses were attributed to compromised infrastructure and developer tools rather than audited smart contracts.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Q3's $1.2B in crypto hacks driven by compromised infrastructure rather than audited smart contracts shifts the underwriting focus from code verification to operational security and vendor due diligence, a more expensive and less scalable problem for the industry.

deals.summary: Binance.US is reportedly seeking a $1 billion valuation as it explores a potential $100 million funding round. This move comes as the exchange navigates ongoing regulatory challenges in the United States.

Payward, the parent company of Kraken, has agreed to acquire Lithuania-based Saldo Bank. This move marks the first time a crypto firm has purchased a European bank to integrate traditional banking services with digital asset offerings.

TD Cowen has raised its price target for Strive by 27% following the company's aggressive Bitcoin acquisition strategy. Strive is planning a $630 million preferred share offering to further fund its Bitcoin purchases.
Nasdaq-listed Tron Inc. has established a $200 million at-the-market (ATM) share offering. The company intends to use the net proceeds from this program to acquire more TRX tokens.

Polygon Labs has finalized the acquisition of Coinme to enhance its stablecoin payments infrastructure. This move provides Polygon with necessary licenses and exemptions to operate across 48 US states.

Tether and HIVEN have acted as strategic investors to complete a seed extension funding round for AIsa. This move signals Tether's continued expansion into strategic investments beyond its core stablecoin business.

on_the_radar.title: EU authority classifies Circle’s USDC as ‘significant’ under MiCA
on_the_radar.summary: The European Union has classified Circle's USDC as a 'significant' e-money token under the Markets in Crypto Assets (MiCA) framework. USDC is the first asset to receive this specific designation among 45 other classified offerings.

on_the_radar.title: BNY, Citadel Securities complete Treasury repo in first use of tokenized assets on major triparty platform
on_the_radar.summary: BNY and Citadel Securities have successfully completed a Treasury repo using tokenized assets on a major triparty platform. The transaction involved a tokenized 2-year U.S. Treasury that settled in minutes on BNY's private ledger.

on_the_radar.title: Evernorth taps Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase and BitGo to put $648 million XRP treasury to work
on_the_radar.summary: Evernorth is partnering with Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase, and BitGo to manage and deploy a $648 million XRP treasury. The company plans to implement institutional strategies and eventually expand into lending and credit markets on the XRP Ledger.

on_the_radar.title: Russia clears Sberbank for crypto trading ahead of December launch17m, Russia clears Sberbank for crypto trading ahead of December launchRussia’s largest bank, Sberbank, has secured crypto exchange authorization as it prepares to offer Bitcoin, Ether and Tether USDt trading.
on_the_radar.summary: Russia's largest bank, Sberbank, has received official authorization to operate as a crypto exchange. The bank plans to launch trading services for Bitcoin, Ether, and Tether USDt in December.

on_the_radar.title: Cysic crypto bridge halted after unauthorized mint of 10M CYS44m
on_the_radar.summary: Cysic has halted its crypto bridge following an unauthorized minting of 10 million CYS tokens. The exploit resulted in a loss of approximately $44 million.

on_the_radar.title: Chinese suspect in $75M international crime network arrested in Bangkok
on_the_radar.summary: Thai authorities in Bangkok have arrested a Chinese suspect linked to an international crime network involved in laundering $75 million. The operation highlights the ongoing use of digital assets to facilitate large-scale illicit financial flows.

on_the_radar.title: Turkey confirms Hex founder Richard Heart's arrest, says police seized $7.15 million and six cold wallets
on_the_radar.summary: Turkish authorities have confirmed the arrest of Hex founder Richard Heart, along with his wife and bodyguards. Police seized $7.15 million in assets and six cold wallets during the operation.

on_the_radar.title: Lagarde says euro-area economy is resilient, digital euro imminent
on_the_radar.summary: ECB President Christine Lagarde stated that the euro-area economy remains resilient and indicated that the launch of the digital euro is imminent. This signals a major step forward in the European Union's transition toward a centralized digital currency.

on_the_radar.title: Circle details USDC revenue split, says $819 million went to partners and costs in H1 2026
on_the_radar.summary: Circle provided a detailed breakdown of USDC revenue for H1 2026, noting that $819 million was allocated to partners and operational costs. The report highlights USDC's dominant market position, capturing 77% of global stablecoin transaction volume in June.

on_the_radar.title: Deutsche Bank prepares German crypto custody launch, eyes Asia: Report 14m
on_the_radar.summary: Deutsche Bank is preparing to launch a cryptocurrency custody service in Germany and is exploring expansion into Asian markets. This move signals a significant step toward institutional crypto adoption by one of Europe's largest banks.

on_the_radar.title: The OCC Report Says Operation Choke Point 2.0 Was Real
on_the_radar.summary: An OCC report validates crypto industry claims regarding 'Operation Choke Point 2.0,' finding that major banks used vague reputational-risk standards to deny services to crypto firms. This confirmation provides regulatory backing to the industry's concerns over systemic banking exclusion.

on_the_radar.title: Visa Direct moves USDC prefunding into commercial production with Inyo Global
on_the_radar.summary: Visa Direct has moved its USDC prefunding service into commercial production in partnership with Inyo Global. This allows eligible payment companies to facilitate international payouts 24/7 via Inyo's APIs.

linkedin_post:
We assumed the physical device was the one part we didn't have to verify. The $91M Ledger reseller theft through CryptoBilis proves otherwise: tampered hardware with hidden implants captured recovery phrases at factory-adjacent scale, and the attackers didn't need to exploit a single line of smart contract code.

This is not a consumer education problem. Ledger itself described the USB-like password reader attack as one of the most sophisticated the industry has encountered. When physical supply chain compromise rivals Bitget-level infrastructure exploits, the entire custody stack requires repricing.

The contrast with institutional progress is sharp. Mastercard is now integrating stablecoin balances into traditional banking rails. Circle's USDC just became the EU's first 'significant' e-money token under direct EBA reserve oversight from November 12. These moves build compliant infrastructure that abstracts blockchain complexity entirely.

What we are underwriting: whether value capture shifts to distribution and compliance layers while hardware wallet TAM compresses until cryptographic device verification becomes standard. The test is whether Ledger and competitors can deploy factory-to-unboxing attestation before the next reseller compromise.

Retail trusted hardware. That assumption just cost $91 million.
